title: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-calendars companion spec
description:
Define a new JMAP Chat Calendars companion spec (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-calendars-00) for deep calendar integration using JMAP Calendars (draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26).

The original near-term portion of this epic (registering urn:jmap:chat:cap:calendar-event and urn:jmap:chat:cap:availability under Endpoint.type and MessageAction.type) is already present in the main draft (line 224-225 of draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md, since the initial scaffolding commit 20a7b81). MessageAction.type :252 explicitly inherits the Endpoint type URI namespace, so the URN values are valid for both. No further work needed at the URN-registration level.

OUTSTANDING WORK (companion-spec design)

Four design topics, each with open sub-decisions that need direction before a sub-bead can be filed:

1. RSVP-as-reaction mapping
- Map calendar RSVP states (accepted / declined / tentative) onto reactions: specific emoji set? new reaction subtype? new Reaction.metadata field?
- Round-trip: a reaction "I'm in" must turn into a calendar-level RSVP state on the underlying CalendarEvent. Who writes back to the event — the chat server or the calendar server (potentially via JMAP-Calendars CalendarEventNotification)?
- Federation: does the RSVP propagate via Peer/deliver reactionUpdate, or via the JMAP Calendars federation path?

2. Space-level shared calendar
- One calendar per Space, or many? New spaceCalendarId field on Space, or new SpaceCalendar object?
- Who can add events? Mapping to closed Space-permission vocabulary, or new permission (manage_calendar)?
- Who can edit/cancel others' events? RSVP-eligible scope: members, role-filtered, anyone?
- Privacy: are Space members' calendars visible to one another by default?

3. .ics attachment parsing
- Server-side parse or client-side? Trust model — does parsing a peer-supplied .ics and auto-creating a CalendarEvent require consent?
- Failure mode for malformed .ics (reject vs. attach without parse)?
- Quota for auto-created CalendarEvents per chat per hour?

4. Principal/getAvailability in Space context
- Privacy model: who sees whose availability? Account-level default, per-Space override, per-pairing?
- Federation: cross-server availability disclosure by default or only on explicit consent?
- Granularity (free/busy only, or also calendar event summaries)?

Decomposes naturally into one design-decision bead (ffq.1, like fig9.1) followed by one or more implementation beads once the decisions land. Implementation may also gate on draft-ietf-jmap-calendars reaching a stable enough version to depend on.

P4: not urgent. The URN-registration work that would have been the near-term win is already done; what remains is substantial design and probably waits on appetite and on the JMAP Calendars upstream draft.
notes: Aspirational placeholder. Near-term action (adding urn:jmap:chat:cap:calendar-event and urn:jmap:chat:cap:availability to well-known MessageAction and Endpoint types) is already covered by jmap-chat-spec-owe. Full companion spec is speculative — only pursue if there is a concrete deployment need for deep calendar integration.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 91a47d2 (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-calendars-00.md, 354 lines) plus cross-reference updates in 219b9ee. Design decisions made autonomously per Mark's direction: be inspired by fielded systems (Discord Scheduled Events, Microsoft Teams meetings, Slack calendar integrations) but do not over-constrain; use the c93e545/38055ec impl-defined latitude pattern for permission policy.
